summary: Exercise one compliant particle mesh with pinned boundaries, explicit timestep/substeps/iterations and residuals rather than treating visual softness as a material measurement.
objective: Build a bounded XPBD fixture where I change compliance or solver budget, apply a known load and inspect constraint residual, energy proxy and reset.
example_prompts: Pin one side of a tetrahedral sample, apply gravity, then compare residuals when compliance and solver budget change.
negative_signals: Not FEM validation, Young modulus measurement, cloth generalization or production stability guarantee.
not_for: No fracture, plasticity, self collision, fluid coupling, remeshing or universal convergence threshold.

entities.name: Rest mesh and pins
entities.guidance: Blender authors a valid tetrahedral rest fixture, edge topology and named pinned vertex group; Three.js/solver copies positions, masses, rest edge lengths and rest signed volumes into authoritative arrays.

entities.name: Residual fixture
entities.guidance: Show rest/current wireframes, pins, force arrow, maximum normalized constraint residual and exact solver budget.

state_contract.model: Use a finite tetrahedral particle fixture with positive masses or infinite-mass pinned particles, fixed frame step dt, S>=1 substeps of h=dt/S and I>=1 Gauss-Seidel iterations per substep. Declare edge-distance constraints C_edge=|xi-xj|-Lij and signed tetra-volume constraints C_vol=V(x)-V0 with separate nonnegative compliance values whose units follow each C. At each substep predict x_tilde=x+h*v+h^2*M^-1*f_ext, initialize every lambda_j=0, then iterate delta_lambda=(-Cj-alpha_tilde*lambda_j)/(gradC*M^-1*gradC^T+alpha_tilde), delta_x=M^-1*gradC^T*delta_lambda with alpha_tilde=alpha_j/h^2. After projection set v=(x_new-x_old)/h. Accumulate lambda only within the substep; warm starting is outside this recipe. Reject zero denominator, non-finite state and nonpositive signed tetra volume.
state_contract.authority: The selected external solver module owns particle state, constraints, multipliers, forces and fixed-step loop. Three.js owns adapter/history/diagnostics and renders state; Blender owns rest topology and pin labels.
actions: Apply/remove one declared load and advance one substep.
Change compliance, substeps or iterations and start a fresh comparable run.
Inspect per-constraint residuals and inversion flags.
Reset positions, velocities and multipliers to the exact fixture.

invariants: Pinned particles remain at rest coordinates within tolerance.
Every accepted denominator is positive and finite.
Solver-budget changes are recorded with results and never relabeled as material changes.
Each substep starts with zero multipliers; reset additionally clears positions, velocities, multipliers and pending forces to the exact fixture.
motion_guidance: Play, pause and step advance the declared model clock only; reset restores parameters, state, solver budget, selections, errors and presentation transforms.
Use static before/after states and numeric tables for reduced motion; animation interpolates committed state and never supplies physical evidence.
creative_affordances: Blender may shape distinctive apparatus, cutaways and materials; Three.js binds named parts to authoritative state and keeps units and error states readable.
Camera, color, trails and deformation gain are presentation controls and cannot change the numerical model.
known_limits: One tetrahedral fixture with edge-distance and signed-volume XPBD constraints; compliance units differ with the constraint definition, and finite solver budgets retain residual/error. This is not FEM or measured-material equivalence.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no Blender export, numerical simulation, contact solve, browser or renderer was run.

claims.statement: XPBD introduces compliance as inverse stiffness, scales it by inverse squared timestep, accumulates a total Lagrange multiplier, and updates each constraint through the documented delta-lambda and mass-weighted position equations.
claims.scope: Macklin, Müller and Chentanez 2016 XPBD scalar-constraint update; concrete constraint units remain implementation-specific.

claims.statement: The XPBD paper addresses PBD stiffness dependence on timestep and iteration count, but its algorithm is still an iterative solve with approximations and finite residual; this recipe therefore records solver budget and does not assert identical finite-run states.
claims.scope: Documented motivation and algorithm boundary, without a universal convergence or material-validation claim.

source_refs.locator: Abstract, Introduction, equations 15–18 and stated approximations

object_craft.structure: Use a coarse inspectable volume/surface cage, explicit fixed pin fixtures and ghosted rest edges; separate render skin from solver nodes if used.
object_craft.material: Pins, free nodes, inverted cells and residual severity use redundant glyphs and labels.

physical_contract.scope: Finite XPBD particle/constraint fixture with external forces and pinned boundary.
physical_contract.timestep: Fixed dt split into declared substeps and iteration count; record budget with every result.
state: masses, pins, rest edges/volumes, two constraint compliances and per-substep multipliers
colliders: optional declared static plane only; no self collision
driving: gravity or one bounded applied force
contact: only if explicit plane constraint is included
